2027-01-30.title: Saturday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: He looked forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people
Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
2027-01-30.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 3 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary may be celebrated (white).
2027-01-30.verse: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
theo: Hebrews 11 is the great chapter of faith: “Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.” Abraham “set out, not knowing where he was going.” He lived in tents in the promised land, “for he looked forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.” Sarah, past the age, “considered him faithful who had promised.” And when tested, Abraham offered Isaac, reasoning “that God is able even to raise someone from the dead”. Faith is not certainty about the road; it is trust in the One who calls.

In the Gospel the disciples cross the lake at evening. A great windstorm arises; the boat is filling with water; and Jesus is asleep on the cushion in the stern. “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?” He rises, rebukes the wind, says to the sea, “Peace! Be still!”, and there is a dead calm. Then he asks: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?” They are filled with awe: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” Jesus asleep in the storm is not indifferent; he is the Lord of creation, and his presence in the boat is enough. With Mary, who believed without seeing, we learn to trust.
outline: Ask: when has life felt like a boat in a storm?
Not knowing where he was going.
“Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
live: Name your current storm and hand it to Jesus in prayer.
Take one step God is asking of you without knowing the whole road.
2027-01-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you calmed the wind and the sea with a word. In the storms of our lives, give us the faith of Abraham, who set out not knowing where he was going, and the trust of Mary, who believed your word. Peace! Be still! Amen.
altar: At every Mass the Lord who calmed the storm is with us in the boat of the Church, and says: peace be with you.

quick: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
Abraham set out not knowing where he was going.
Jesus calmed the storm: Why are you afraid?
2027-01-30.action: Hand your current storm to Jesus in prayer.
2027-01-30.question: Do I believe Jesus cares when he seems asleep?

family.explain: A big storm came while Jesus was sleeping in the boat. The disciples were scared. Jesus woke up and said: Peace! Be still! And the storm stopped!
family.intention: We pray for those going through hard times.
family.ask: Ask: “When are you scared? Let us ask Jesus to calm our hearts.”

illus: During the 2018 floods in Kerala, a family in Chengannur spent two nights on their roof. The grandmother kept saying the words of Jesus: Peace! Be still! When a fishing boat from the coast rescued them, the fishermen told them they had come because they could not sit still at home. She said: the Lord was in that boat too.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are in our boat. Calm our fears and increase our faith. Amen.
share: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for (Hebrews 11:1). What do I hope for?
He set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). What step is God asking of me?
Why are you afraid? (Mark 4:40). What fear do I need to give to Jesus?
interc: For those in the storms of illness, debt or grief.
For fishermen and sailors at sea.
For refugees and migrants who set out not knowing where they go.
For those who feel God is asleep.
For our group, that we may trust like Mary.
pm.close: Father, your Son calmed the storm. Calm our hearts and deepen our faith, through the prayers of the Virgin Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews gives us the definition of faith: now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1).

Abraham set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). He looked forward to the city whose architect and builder is God. Faith is not knowing the whole road; it is trusting the One who calls.

In the Gospel a great storm arises and Jesus is asleep. The disciples cry: teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? He rises and says: Peace! Be still! Then he asks: why are you afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:38–40).
Jesus asleep in the boat is not indifferent; he is the Lord of wind and sea. With Mary, who believed without seeing, let us trust him in our storms. Amen.
kids: Children, when a big storm came, Jesus said: Peace! Be still! and the storm stopped. When you are scared, say: Jesus, I trust in you!

intro: Theme: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
Faith that sets out, and faith in the storm.

q: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight.
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
points.apply: Make an act of faith each morning.

q: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Take one step of trust God asks of you.

q: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
He woke up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” Then the wind ceased, and there was a dead calm.
points.apply: Hand your storm to Jesus in prayer tonight.

concl: Faith trusts the One who calls, not the map of the road.
The Lord is in our boat.
2027-01-30.resolve: Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” whenever you are afraid.
